docs.title: What to Upload
docs.text:
Credo Analytics supports the following file formats, which you can export directly from your Credo Bank account:

  • .XLSX (Excel): Recommended for detailed transaction data.
  • .PDF: Bank statements in PDF format.
  • .CSV: Comma-separated values (if available).

[!TIP] You can upload multiple files at once. Whether you have monthly statements for the past year or multiple accounts, drag them all into the upload zone together. The application will automatically merge and deduplicate transactions.

docs.title: How to Upload
docs.text:
1. Locate your files: Ensure you have your exported bank statements ready on your device.
  2. Drag & Drop: Simply drag the file(s) from your file explorer and drop them onto the upload area.
  3. Or Click to Browse: Click the upload button to open your system's file picker and select the files you wish to analyze.

The application will instantly parse the files and present your dashboard.

docs.title: Privacy & Security
docs.text: We understand that financial data is sensitive. That's why Credo Analytics is built with a Local-First architecture.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• No Server Uploads: When you "upload" a file, it is read directly by your web browser using JavaScript. The file contents never leave your computer.
  • No Database: There is no backend database storing your transactions. Everything resides in your browser's temporary memory or local storage.
  • Offline Capable: Once the page is loaded, you can disconnect from the internet and the application will continue to function perfectly.

docs.title: How to Verify
docs.text: To prove that your data is safe, you can try this simple test: 1. Open Credo Analytics. 2. Disconnect your internet (turn off Wi-Fi or unplug your Ethernet cable). 3. Upload your bank statements. 4. Watch as the dashboard populates and analysis works flawlessly—without any network connection!

docs.title: Clearing Data
docs.text: If you want to remove all traces of your data from the browser, simply click the Reset Data (Trash Icon) button in the dashboard header. This will wipe the local storage and return the app to its initial state.

docs.title: All Time Stats
docs.text: The All Time view is the default landing page after uploading your files. It aggregates every single transaction to show your complete financial picture.

docs.title: Total Income & Expense
docs.text: The absolute sum of all money coming in (credits) versus money going out (debits). This gives you the scale of your financial activity over the entire period.

docs.title: Net Result
docs.text: The difference between Total Income and Total Expense. * Positive (Green): You earned more than you spent. * Negative (Red): You spent more than you earned.

docs.title: Category Breakdown
docs.text: A visual Doughnut Chart showing where your money went. * Interactive: Hover over (or tap) a slice to see the exact amount and percentage. * Click to Drill Down: Clicking a category reveals a list of specific merchants/transactions within that category.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text: Use this view to answer big-picture questions: * "What is my biggest expense category overall?" * "Have I been net positive over the last few years?" * "How much has my total income been since I opened these accounts?"

docs.title: Custom Analysis
docs.text: Need to check a specific event, like a vacation or a project? Use the Custom tab.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The Custom tab gives you full control over the date range.

  1. Select Range: Click "Select Date Range" to open the picker.
  2. Start & End Dates: Choose any start date and end date. The dashboard will instantly recalculate everything—charts, totals, and lists—just for that specific period.
  3. Analyze: Use this filtered view to answer questions like:
    • "How much did my trip to Batumi cost?"
    • "What was my total spending on 'Groceries' during my renovation?"

docs.title: Resetting
docs.text: To clear the custom range, simply switch back to another tab (e.g., All Time or Month). Your custom selection is temporary and specific to this view.

docs.title: Formulas & Calculations
docs.text: Transparency is key. Here acts how Credo Analytics processes your numbers.

docs.title: Total Income
docs.text: $$ \text{Total Income} = \sum (\text{Transactions with Positive Amount}) $$ Includes salaries, transfers in, refunds, etc.

docs.title: Total Expense
docs.text: $$ \text{Total Expense} = \sum (\text{Transactions with Negative Amount}) $$ Includes purchases, bill payments, transfers out, etc.

docs.title: Net Result
docs.text: $$ \text{Net Result} = \text{Total Income} - |\text{Total Expense}| $$ Shows the net change in your wealth for the selected period.

docs.title: Exchange Rates
docs.text: If you have multi-currency accounts (e.g., GEL, USD, EUR): 1. Base Currency: The app defaults to the currency of your first uploaded account (usually GEL). 2. Conversion: Transactions in other currencies are converted to the base currency using the historical exchange rate on the date of the transaction. 3. Source: Exchange rates are fetched from credible financial APIs or estimated based on daily averages if precise data is unavailable.

docs.title: Noise Filter Logic
docs.text:
When the Noise Filter is active (default), the app hides: * Internal Transfers: Money moved between your own accounts (e.g., Checking -> Savings). * Exchange Operations: Buying/selling currency within your accounts.

This ensures your "Income" reflects real earnings and "Expense" reflects real spending, not just moving money around.

docs.title: Time Periods
docs.text: Credo Analytics allows you to break down your data into manageable chunks for better comparisons.

docs.title: Year View
docs.text: View your finances month-by-month for a specific year. * Why use it? Identify seasonal trends (e.g., higher spending in December). * Navigation: Click the < and > arrows next to the year label (e.g., "2024") to switch between years.

docs.title: Month View
docs.text: A detailed breakdown of a single month. * Why use it? Check if you stayed within your budget for the month. * Navigation: Jump between months (e.g., "January", "February") or click the date picker to select a specific month.

docs.title: Week View
docs.text: Analyze your spending week-by-week. * Why use it? Spot weekly habits, like weekend spending spikes. * Navigation: Move between weeks (e.g., "Week 4") or select a week from the calendar.

docs.title: Day View
docs.text: Zoom into a single day's transactions. * Why use it? Audit specific days or trace individual transactions.

docs.title: Navigation Controls
docs.text: When you select a period (other than All Time), a navigation bar appears: * Left Arrow (←): Go to the previous period (e.g., Previous Month). * Center Label: Displays the current period. Click to open a Date Picker for quick selection. * Right Arrow (→): Go to the next period (e.g., Next Month).

docs.title: Main Dashboard
docs.text: The dashboard is designed to give you both a high-level overview and deep insights into your finances.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
The interface is divided into key sections:

  1. Header: Global controls and file management.
  2. Account Information: Located just below the title, this shows the account holder name and a summary of loaded accounts (e.g., "3 accounts · 2× GEL + USD").
  3. Period Navigation: Tabs to switch between All Time, Year, Month, Week, Day, and Custom.
  4. Summary & Charts: The main content area, which updates based on the selected period.

docs.title: Mobile Experience
docs.text:
Unlike traditional banking apps that often feel cramped, Credo Analytics is optimized for mobile devices.

  • Stacking: On smaller screens, the layout automatically adjusts. Side-by-side elements like charts and lists stack vertically for easier reading.
  • Touch-Friendly: Buttons and interactive elements are sized for touch targets.
  • Collapsible Sections: In lists (like Category Breakdown), details are hidden by default to save space but can be expanded with a tap.

docs.title: Currency Handling
docs.text: If your uploaded files contain multiple currencies (e.g., GEL and USD transactions), a Currency Toggle will appear in the top right. * Click a currency code (e.g., USD) to convert all charts and totals to that currency. * The application uses historical exchange rates to provide accurate conversions at the time of each transaction.

docs.title: Dashboard Header
docs.text: The header is your control center for Credo Analytics. It provides quick access to global settings and privacy tools.

docs.title: Controls Overview
docs.text: Icon/Button Name Function Theme Toggle Light/Dark Mode Switches the interface between a bright, clean look and a dark, eye-friendly theme. Language English/Russian Toggles the interface language. Eye Icon Privacy Mode Blurs all sensitive monetary values on the screen. Useful when sharing your screen or working in public. Filter Icon Noise Filter Hides internal transfers (e.g., self-transfers between your own accounts) to show only "real" spending and income. Add Files Add More Data Allows you to upload additional statements to merge with your current data. Trash Icon Reset Data Completely clears all transaction data from the browser and returns you to the welcome screen.

docs.title: Date Range & Transaction Count
docs.text:
In the top left, under the title, you will see a summary of your loaded data: * Date Range: The start and end dates of all transactions currently loaded. * Transaction Count: The total number of transactions being analyzed.

This quick summary helps you verify that you've uploaded all the necessary files for the period you want to analyze.
